back: 1) Pericarditis (most common cardiac manifestation). 2) Libman-Sacks endocarditis (sterile verrucous vegetations on valves). 3) Coronary vasculitis / accelerated atherosclerosis. 4) Myocarditis.

front: Which sero-negative rheumatologic disease classically causes aortic root dilation and AR?
back: Ankylosing spondylitis (and related seronegative spondyloarthritis). Also causes conduction disease (AV block).

front: Which two valves are typically affected by carcinoid heart disease, and how?
back: Tricuspid valve and pulmonic valve — thickened, retracted, immobile leaflets producing mixed regurgitation and stenosis. Left-sided involvement only occurs with a right-to-left shunt (PFO) or bronchial carcinoid.

front: Marfan syndrome — genetic basis and classic cardiovascular echo findings?
back: Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) mutation on chromosome 15. Findings: aortic root (sinus of Valsalva) dilation, mitral valve prolapse, sometimes tricuspid prolapse. Extracardiac: ectopia lentis, tall stature.

front: How does Loeys-Dietz syndrome differ from Marfan?
back: Loeys-Dietz: TGFβ receptor mutations. More aggressive aortic dilation and earlier surgical thresholds (root repair at smaller diameters). Characteristic bifid uvula, hypertelorism, arterial tortuosity throughout body.

front: Chagas cardiomyopathy — classic echo and ECG features?
back: Apical LV aneurysm (dyskinetic apex with preserved basal function) plus conduction disease (RBBB + left anterior fascicular block). Caused by chronic Trypanosoma cruzi infection.
Initially restrictive phenotype from myocardial iron deposition, later transitioning to dilated cardiomyopathy. Cardiac T2* by cMRI is the gold-standard imaging biomarker.

front: Which endocrine disorder classically causes a pericardial effusion, bradycardia, and diastolic dysfunction?

back: High-output state, sinus tachycardia or atrial fibrillation, functional mitral regurgitation from annular dilation, and (long-term) LV dysfunction from tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Dilated cardiomyopathy (viral or antiretroviral toxicity), pericardial effusion, pulmonary hypertension, accelerated coronary artery disease.
